audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Tryndamere four of seven stages in a lane he wins 48.8% of, and disagree with the already-audited mirror.
audit.why: The mirrored gragas__tryndamere audit set both layers to Skill, Gragas, Skill, Gragas, Gragas, Gragas, Tryndamere. Body Slam is a 14s stun that is also his escape, so the levels where Tryndamere has no answer to it are his, and only the two-item split window comes back.
audit.corrected: Skill, Gragas, Skill, Gragas, Gragas, Gragas, Tryndamere — proposed as one atomic full/content group with ratings inverted to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere; the level-6 spike was written as a clean Tryndamere win.
audit.why: Body Slam 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s — it barely improves with rank, which is the whole reason baiting it works all game. Barrel Roll 10/9/8/7/6s at 80 mana flat. Drunken Rage 5s. Explosive Cask 100/85/70s. Undying Rage 120/100/80s.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into spikes, breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: The page claimed Undying Rage 'neutralizes his Explosive Cask burst' and told you to 'tank the knock with your ult'. Surviving the damage is not the same as resisting the knockback.
audit.why: Riot's text: Explosive Cask 'deals damage and knocks back enemies caught in the blast radius'. Undying Rage prevents death; it grants no displacement immunity in Riot's text. Being thrown out of auto range is exactly how a Gragas beats an immortal Tryndamere — he does not need to kill you, only to move you.
audit.corrected: Explosive Cask knocks you back even while Undying Rage is up — immortal is not unstoppable.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] credited Gragas with 'passive shielding'. Happy Hour is a heal, and the damage reduction comes from Drunken Rage.
audit.why: Riot: 'Gragas periodically heals upon using a skill' (P); Drunken Rage's empowered attack also 'reduc[es] damage received'. Two different mechanics, and the one that matters for your build is the heal — it makes Grievous Wounds timing decide the extended trade.
audit.corrected: Happy Hour heals him every time he casts and Drunken Rage cuts the damage he takes — buy Executioner's.

audit.whatIsWrong: Drunken Rage's auto-attack reset was never mentioned.
audit.why: The combo lands on the swing after the 1-second sample, not on the cast — the wind-up is the cue to step out.
audit.corrected: Drunken Rage is an auto reset on a 5s cooldown — step off on the wind-up.

edits.after: At 4-5 Barrel Roll drops toward 7s and Happy Hour heals him through your chip trades.

edits.before: At level 6 R Undying Rage nullifies his Cask kill pattern, so the spike is yours.
edits.after: At 6 Explosive Cask knocks you out of range and his 100s ult beats your window.

edits.after: At first item his burst plus Happy Hour outpaces your pre-crit damage.

edits.before: With E Spinning Slash you can gap-close onto Gragas the instant his Body Slam E is down — that dash is his only escape and disengage, so bait it or wait it out, then Q-fueled all-in while he has no bump.
edits.after: Body Slam is 14s at rank 1 and barely drops with rank — 12s at rank 5 — and it is both his engage and his only escape. It also stuns, so it beats your spin in a straight race. Commit only after he spends it.

edits.before: R Undying Rage beats his kill pattern cleanly: even if he lands Explosive Cask R to knock you around, you pop your immortality, keep autoing, and heal back up with Q before he can reset his cooldowns.
edits.after: Undying Rage stops the death but not the displacement — Explosive Cask still knocks you out of range, and time spent flying is time not autoing. Hold your ult until after the Cask lands; his is 100s at rank 1.

edits.before: You out-scale his damage hard once you have crit — Gragas is a tanky mage with no reliable single-target kill on you, so a Botrk/IE spike lets you shred him through his passive shielding.
edits.after: Happy Hour heals him every time he casts and Drunken Rage cuts the damage he takes — that pair, not armour, is what survives your crits. Buy Executioner's before you try to burst him down.

edits.before: With crit items online you dominate the 1v1 — R Undying Rage neutralizes his Explosive Cask burst, so E onto him or his backline, tank the knock with your ult, and heal through his kit while your autos delete him.
edits.after: With crit online you win the 1v1, but only on clean ground — Explosive Cask displaces you whether or not your ult is up, so spin in after he throws it. Drunken Rage is an auto reset on a 5s cooldown — step off on the wind-up.

edits.before: - Gragas Body Slam: matchup-defining — His engage. E-spin away from it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Body Slam (E): 14s at rank 1, only 12s at rank 5 — his engage, his escape, and a stun. - Barrel Roll (Q): 10s down to 6s, 80 mana flat. - Explosive Cask: 100s at rank 1 — it displaces you through your ult.

edits.after: Barrel Roll grows stronger the longer it sits — never stand on it.

notes: The packet's suspectName is a false positive: wants.foe[2] writes 'Land Explosive Cask R to knock you away from him' and Explosive Cask is the correct name for Gragas's R. No change made there. Left alone: diff is 'EVEN' with diffRating 6/10 and report[14] 'Even matchup' while the win rate is 48.8% and the chart now gives Gragas four of seven stages — the enum may warrant a downgrade, but I do not know the vocabulary the applier accepts beyond EVEN/FAV/HARD and did not guess. Also left alone per the mirror: the '5 seconds' duration claimed for Undying Rage is not in Riot's text, so I avoided restating it in any new sentence.
